A small jewel-scaled fae dragon, no bigger than a deer, glides silently over the city's spires.
A great low luminous moon hangs behind the towers, vast and silver, doubling in the lake below.
A slow fall of cherry blossom drifts down across the white bridges and walkways, catching the light.
A flight of white swans crosses the sky above the tallest spire, wings catching the golden hour.
An aurora spills over the city in slow green and violet curtains, reflected in every canal below.
An elven boat glides the still water, a single glowing lantern casting amber rings across the surface.
A shaft of divine light breaks through the forest canopy, falling like a column onto the central plaza.
A unicorn stands in the garden below, white and still, luminous as carved moonstone among the blossoms.
A procession of fae lights drifts along the high bridges, small and warm as scattered embers in the dark.
A rainbow arches over the waterfall at the city's edge, vivid and trembling in the rising mist.
A comet drags its pale fire across the twilight above the towers, slow and breathtaking in the deep blue.
A phoenix passes overhead, trailing embers like a living torch, its reflection blazing briefly in the water.
Golden autumn leaves spiral down in slow eddies across the lantern-lit walkways and pale stone balustrades.
A second flight of swans descends toward the lake, their white wings mirrored in the glassy stillness below.
A jewel-green fae dragon circles the highest tower twice, then vanishes into the rose-gold light beyond.
The full moon rises enormous and amber behind the eastern spires, enormous as a second sun setting.
Fae lantern-lights drift upward from the bridges like released breath, rising slowly into the violet evening sky.
A wide aurora blooms overhead in rose and pale gold, soft as silk laid across the dark firmament.
Cherry blossom and golden leaves fall together in one brief impossible drift across the ancient silver stairways.
The elven boat returns at dusk, its lantern doubled in the water, a quiet ember on the dark lake.
A unicorn moves slowly through the terraced garden, pausing once, its horn briefly bright against the shadowed hedge.
Divine light pours through a gap in the high canopy, illuminating one white tower in perfect silence.
A comet burns low and long across the horizon, just above the spires, leaving a faint trail of silver.
The phoenix circles the waterfall once, and where its feathers brush the mist, brief roses of fire bloom.
A procession of fae lights rounds the uppermost bridge, delicate as breathing, steady as stars finding their places.
